finding.why: iCCP + tEXt + tIME are ancillary metadata the GPU never uses; 8347 >= minBytes 4096 (fires) and < warnBytes 65536 (info). The iCCP is PROVABLY sRGB (profile name 'sRGB IEC61966-2.1' matches /srgb/i) so its 8227 bytes stay a free strip — removing an sRGB profile does not change colours. pHYs is NOT counted (a re-encoder keeps it). DISK only — invariant 5.

The iCCP (Display P3) is NOT provably sRGB, so its 3024 bytes are EXCLUDED from strippableBytes — removing a non-sRGB profile would shift the rendered colours, so it is not a free saving. Only the tEXt (62 B) remains, which is < minBytes 4096, so the strippable-metadata finding does NOT fire.

iccFinding.why: A DISCLOSURE/correctness finding: this PNG embeds an ICC profile we cannot prove is sRGB. It carries NO estimate (no diskBytesSaved, no vramBytesSaved) — precedent: texture-bleeding, dimension-mismatch. We measure and disclose; the Pro strip fix keeps the chunk (keepIcc).

note: TWO hand-authored, REAL valid 4x4 RGBA8888 PNGs for the strippable-metadata detector AND the icc-non-srgb honesty rule. metadata.png embeds a PROVABLY-sRGB iCCP (profile name 'sRGB IEC61966-2.1') + tEXt + tIME (8347 strippable) + a pHYs that is DELIBERATELY NOT counted; the iCCP bytes stay counted because a provably-sRGB profile is a free strip. metadata-p3.png embeds a NON-provable iCCP ('Display P3', no sRGB chunk): its 3024 iCCP bytes are EXCLUDED from strippableBytes (removing a non-sRGB profile shifts colours — invariant 3), leaving only 62 tEXt bytes (below minBytes ⇒ strippable does not fire) and firing the icc-non-srgb disclosure (info; NO estimate). The counted allow-set remains a conservative TRUE LOWER BOUND of what the existing Pro fix removes (README, Test D).
